comparisons.peer_summary: Client operating income improved to an $897 million profit in 2024 from a $46 million operating loss in 2023, primarily due to higher revenue partially offset by higher operating expenses.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD report specific segment revenue and profitability improvements in fiscal 2024 driven primarily by higher revenue volumes. QCOM attributes its QCT revenue increase to higher chipset shipments from major OEMs, while AMD attributes its Client segment operating income improvement to higher revenue. However, the magnitude and context differ: QCOM highlights a specific $2.8 billion shipment increase alongside unfavorable mix pressure (-$533M), whereas AMD reports a shift from a loss to a significant profit ($897M) without detailing specific volume drivers in the same granularity.

sentences.text: The increase in QCT revenues in fiscal 2024 was primarily due to:

+ higher handsets revenues, due to $2.8 billion in higher chipset shipments driven by certain major OEMs (primarily driven by the normalization of customer inventory levels, which were elevated in the prior year), partially offset by $533 million in lower revenues per chipset primarily driven by unfavorable mix
Client operating income was $897 million in 2024, compared to operating loss of $46 million in 2023.
The increase in operating income was primarily due to higher revenue, partially offset by higher operating expenses.

comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue increased to 49% in 2024 from 46% in 2023. This increase was primarily driven by a favorable shift in revenue mix towards higher Data Center and Client revenues, as well as lower Gaming revenue, which was partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies explain margin improvements in FY2024 by citing favorable revenue mix shifts. QCOM's QCT EBT margin increase is linked to higher revenues, while AMD explicitly attributes its gross margin expansion (49% vs 46%) to a favorable shift towards higher-value Data Center and Client revenues. Both disclosures identify product mix as a key positive driver for profitability metrics in the current year.

sentences.text: QCT EBT as a percentage of revenues increased in fiscal 2024 primarily due to higher revenues.
Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue was 49% in 2024 compared to 46% in 2023.
The increase in gross margin was due to a favorable shift in revenue mix of higher Data Center and Client revenues, lower Gaming revenue, partially offset by the impact of lower Embedded revenue.

comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AVGO report segment operating income increases driven by specific product category growth. QCOM's QCT segment grew due to handset and automotive product launches (Snapdragon digital cockpit), while AVGO's semiconductor solutions segment grew primarily due to networking products, specifically AI networking products. Both disclosures highlight the positive impact of specific high-demand product lines on their respective segment profitability.

Both disclosures use the 'driven by [growth area], partially offset by [decline area]' structure to explain net segment performance.
